base.description: Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. The 4 slot bays are EMPTY; cooling, psus, res are populated. Enough to power on and reach the box, which is the question most people ask first and the one `default` used to answer with whatever the drawing happened to be populated with. The line-card slots are drawn EMPTY rather than blanked, which is not the intent: no MX10000-series line-card blank is modelled, and none is named in the staged guides - they document power-supply cover panels only. Every other chassis in the library seats a blank here.
base.source: vendor - Juniper publishes this as an orderable bundle. the hardware guide's 'MX10004 Configurations' section lists the components of each configuration, and the line-card covers in this base are its own: it ships sixteen of them on the MX10016 in EVERY configuration, over the note that "Line cards and the cable management system are not part of the base or redundant configurations. You must order them separately." NOT YET FULLY FAITHFUL: the vendor bundle also ships ONE routing engine rather than two, and covers rather than modules in one SFB slot and one power slot. This library seats all of them, because JNP10K-PWR-BLNK and the SF blank are not modelled yet. The line-card half - the part that was drawing holes - is now right.

description: Juniper MX10004 - the 7RU, four-slot member of the MX10000 family. Two slim Routing and Control Boards stack under the badge strip beside the system status lamp panel; four full-width horizontal line-card slots (FPC 0-3) fill the lower front. The rear is a three-high PSU stack (PSU 0-2) beside two large fan trays whose removal exposes the six Switch Fabric Boards.

gaps.wanted: a photograph of a real RCB's model label. The board in this chassis's own photographs carries four SFP cages numbered 0-3 and no BITS, ToD, RESET or Online/Offline hardware, which matches neither Juniper faceplate figure - not Figure 46 (JNP10K-RE1 family, two reserved XGE cages) nor Figure 45 (JNP10K-RE3 family). juniper/jnp10k-re1@2 follows the figure it is named for; the detail is in provenance/which-board-the-photographs-show on that contract. The label does not resolve at the scale of any photograph held here.
the JNP10K-PWR-AC3, DC2 and DC3 faces (AC3 adds four feeds A0/A1/B0/B1 and six LEDs; only AC2 is photographed usably).
LC2101, LC4800 and LC4802 faceplates - the guide names them and gives dimensions and power, but the extraction has no usable face art; only LC9600 and LC480 are modelled.
legible FPC slot labels - the top-down 0-3 order follows the family convention, not a readable print.
a vendor dimension for the RCB face - the FRU table covers chassis, cards and PSUs but not the RCB; 389 mm is photo-derived.

attrs.redundancy-note: 1+1 - mx10004 hardware guide, "MX10004 Component Redundancy": one or two RCBs; with two fitted one is primary and the other backup, and the backup takes over if the primary or any part of it fails. The RCB consolidates the Routing Engine function with the control plane function in a single unit, so this one form covers both

power.note: datasheet-table - the guide capacity table: two JNP10K-PWR-AC2 at high power deliver 11,000 W, three 16,500 W. The MX10000 datasheet states typical power consumption 7.5 kW, fully loaded, naming no ambient or side - carried as power-typical-w. Its footnote calling the figures power supply ratings is attached to the power system rating row, not to this one. The guide rates every FRU by ambient (Table 55, including the fan trays: JNP10004-FAN2 651 W, JNP10004-FAN3 880 W) and works an example of 10,082 W for an MX10004-PREMIUM with four MX10K-LC9600 (3002 W + 7080 W) - a sample, not carried
